Consonantal i

Theme

School & learning

conjugation noun

also conjugations, conjugate, conjugate a verb, first conjugation

late Latin

Diom. p. 337 P.; Prisc. p. 836 P. (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 227, 245
M-O s.v. conjugation, after Vives

conjugātiō, conjugātiōnis f.

noun, third declension

a conjugation: a class of verbs inflected alike; the inflection of a verb

A term of the later grammarians (Comminianus in Charisius, Diomedes, Priscian) and of every Latin grammar since: verbum prīmae conjugātiōnis, a verb of the first conjugation (Traupman 227). In Cicero it is the kinship of words from one root (Top. 12, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • dēclīnātiō, dēclīnātiōnis f. — the conjugation of a verb; any inflection

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Quint. 1.4.29: multa verba nōn tōtum dēclīnātiōnis ōrdinem ferunt; Varr. LL 8.2 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 245

    Varro’s and Quintilian’s word for the inflection of verbs as of nouns; Traupman calls it the more common term. To conjugate a verb is verbum dēclīnāre (Quint. 1.4.22; Traupman 227).

Examples

  • quid? quod multa verba nōn tōtum dēclīnātiōnis ōrdinem ferunt? quaedam etiam mūtantur ut ferō in praeteritō

    And what of the many verbs that do not have the whole series of the conjugation? Some even change, as ferō does in the perfectQuint. 1.4.29

  • Dēclīnā verbum āctīvum prīmae conjugātiōnis.

    Conjugate an active verb of the first conjugation.Traupman 227

See also verb, declension, grammar.
